sources.title: Acquisition of Ukrainian Citizenship
sources.officialityEvidence: The current State Migration Service page identifies a passport for travel abroad as a document confirming Ukrainian citizenship.

sources.title: MFA resumes issuing electronic visas (e-Visa) to foreigners
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA's 18 February 2025 notice is live and was crawled three weeks before review. It confirms resumed issuance from 19 February 2025, but says only that the programme covers 45 countries.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Starting from February 19, 2025, the MFA resumes issuance of e-Visas for foreigners from 45 countries.

sources.title: e-Visa
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA e-Visa page was crawled three weeks before review and says electronic visas are issued to foreigners from 43 states, conflicting with the 2025 resumption notice's 45-country statement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: МЗС здійснює централізоване оформлення віз в електронному вигляді іноземцям 43-ти держав світу.

sources.title: Entry regime to Ukraine for foreign citizens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The official MFA page was crawled within two weeks of review and continues to publish the detailed ordinary travel-passport table, but expressly labels it as of 8 June 2023. A later Presidential Decree extends the UK waiver through 30 January 2027, confirming that this is not a current consolidated schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Information on the regime of entry of foreigners into Ukraine, as of June 08, 2023.

sources.title: Extending the duration of stay on the territory of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The current State Migration Service guidance distinguishes visa-based stays from visa-free 90-in-180 stays without publishing a nationality schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: visa-free entry regime may stay temporarily ... up to 90 days during any 180 day period

sources.title: The Ministry of Internal Affairs has developed an algorithm of actions on the entry and stay of foreigners
sources.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry describes entry documentation and conduct under martial law but does not publish nationality-specific visa categories.
sources.supportingExcerpt: taking into account the introduction of martial law in Ukraine

sources.title: Visa information
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MFA visa-information page was crawled three weeks before review. It confirms consular, limited emergency-airport, and electronic processes, but gives only the same unenumerated 45-country e-Visa count.
sources.supportingExcerpt: E-Visas are issued to foreigners-holders of passports of 45 specified countries as single or double entry 30-day visas.

sources.officialityEvidence: The Verkhovna Rada portal publishes the registered MFA order amending the operative e-Visa requirements, including the Annex 3 deletions.

policies.title: Ukrainian ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Ukrainian ordinary-passport traveller is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: This is a narrow catalogue home classification. Martial-law restrictions, military records, dual nationality, residence, work and special-document rules are outside the ordinary foreign-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: current legal electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: The current registered MFA e-Visa requirements expressly name these nationalities in Annex 3. The legally operative schedule has contained 42 names since 25 March 2025, when the MFA removed Grenada, Peru and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; the live MFA page's unenumerated 43-state count is retained as a source discrepancy but does not negate the 42 directly named legal routes.
conditions: This is the directly named ordinary-passport e-Visa eligibility cohort in the registered current legal schedule, not a complement inferred from portal availability or omission.

MFA resumed actual e-Visa issuance on 19 February 2025. The legal Annex 3 has 42 names after its 25 March 2025 amendment, while the live MFA e-Visa page says 43 and the February resumption notice said 45 without a roster; the unidentified count discrepancy is retained and no forty-third nationality is inferred.

An e-Visa may be single or double entry and up to 30 days for the listed visitor purposes. It is issued online before travel; this policy does not establish visa-free, visa-on-arrival, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, third-country-document, carrier, or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: United Kingdom ordinary passports: temporary visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Presidential Decree No. 921/2025 extends visa-free entry and transit for United Kingdom citizens through 30 January 2027 for stays up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The decree applies to citizens of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland for entry and transit, limited to 90 days in any 180-day period.

The Decree entered into force on publication. This ordinary-passport visitor baseline does not establish work, residence, special-document, border-access, carrier, security or final-admission treatment.
